title: Enabling turn-gated control from TermAl takes minutes because every step runs the whole-store doctor audit
outcome: An operator can verify and enable an Engram project in a host in a few seconds on a large store, because the host's enablement check no longer waits for a full-store audit, and it is known what dominates doctor's time on the live store and whether the audit itself can be made faster or incremental.
acceptance: a decision is recorded on what a host needs for enablement (store identity, health, required assurance) and whether that needs the full audit or a fast read such as `control-policy show` plus a bounded health check

after the change, verifying and saving turn-gated control for the Engram project from TermAl completes in seconds and the setting persists, shown by TermAl's saved project settings and a new control session in the store
what dominates `engram doctor --json` on the live Engram store (72 s measured on a 179 MB store) is established by measurement, per phase, and recorded
disposal_reason: Obsolete on Greg's word (Asistant #239): turn-gated control no longer exists, so there is nothing to enable. Doctor's own time on the live store, its third criterion, would be a new item if it still matters.
